effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` RLUSD to the vault (safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets) in enter).
The vault mints previewDeposit(assets) senRLUSDv2 shares to `onBehalf`; the share count comes from the current share price, with no minimum in the call.
The deposited RLUSD may be allocated to the liquidity adapter; this does not change the signer's balances.
formats.shown: Deposit 2 RLUSD for a named address, with the share ticker senRLUSDv2 and the share recipient; the number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many shares the signer receives; the share price sets it and no minimum exists.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. Case 0: signer receives 2000000037999999962 senRLUSDv2; the screen shows only 'Share ticker: senRLUSDv2' and 'Send shares to'.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show a storage-derived share count. Optionally rename 'Share ticker' to 'Receive shares (amount set by share price)'.

findings.title: deposit labels the RLUSD amount 'Deposit asset' when it holds an amount, not an asset.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field `assets`: "label": "Deposit asset", format tokenAmount; case 0 renders 'Deposit asset: 2 RLUSD'.

cases.notes: RLUSD out (2) is shown right. senRLUSDv2 in: ticker and recipient are shown, the amount (2.000000038) is not, and the code sets no bound. The reader knew shares arrive but not how many.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns previewWithdraw(assets) senRLUSDv2 shares from `onBehalf`, rounded up, with no maximum in the call.
If the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer spends that many shares of the owner's share allowance.
`receiver` receives exactly `assets` RLUSD from the vault.
formats.shown: Withdraw an exact RLUSD amount to a named receiver, with the share owner named; the number of shares burned is not shown.

findings.title: withdraw does not show how many senRLUSDv2 shares it burns; the share price sets it with no cap.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)`; exit: `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares);`. Case 2: signer loses 1514166.207643334206842215 senRLUSDv2; the screen shows only 'Withdraw exactly: 1514000 RLUSD' and 'Owner'.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show the computed share count. Optionally add a constant field naming the shares burned, e.g. label 'Shares burned from owner' with value $.metadata.constants.vaultTicker.

cases.notes: RLUSD in (1514000 to the signer) is shown right. Shares out: the owner is shown, but the share token and amount (1514166.2 senRLUSDv2) are not. The reader understood that a position shrinks but not the share token or amount.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` senRLUSDv2 from `onBehalf`.
If the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer spends `shares` of the owner's share allowance.
`receiver` receives previewRedeem(shares) RLUSD; the share price sets the amount and no minimum exists.
formats.shown: Redeem an exact amount of senRLUSDv2 shares to a named receiver, with the owner named; the screen never names RLUSD or an amount received.

findings.title: redeem never names RLUSD as the asset the receiver gets; the reader had to guess it.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` with asset = RLUSD. Descriptor redeem fields: only 'Shares to redeem', 'To', 'Owner'. Case 3: signer receives 173083.456684971756044295 RLUSD; reader: 'Underlying asset (likely RLUSD) ... exact amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field like the mint format: {"label": "Receive asset", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}, and change interpolatedIntent to "Redeem {#.shares} for RLUSD to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: redeem cannot show the RLUSD amount received; the share price sets it and no minimum exists.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. No minAssets parameter.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show it.

cases.notes: Shares out (173087.74 senRLUSDv2) are shown right. RLUSD in: the receiver is shown, but neither the asset nor the amount (173083.46). The reader guessed 'likely RLUSD' with no amount.

effects: The signer pays previewMint(shares) RLUSD to the vault; the share price sets the amount and no maximum exists.
The vault mints exactly `shares` senRLUSDv2 to `onBehalf`.
formats.shown: Mint an exact number of senRLUSDv2 shares for a named address, with 'Deposit asset: RLUSD'; the RLUSD amount paid is not shown.

findings.title: mint intent and sentence say 'Mint' and never say that RLUSD leaves the signer's wallet.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint: "intent": "Mint", "interpolatedIntent": "Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}"; VaultV2.sol enter: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets);`. Case 1: signer sends 0.000000001 RLUSD; screen sentence 'Mint 0.000000001 senRLUSDv2 for 0x...dEaD'.
findings.fix: Change intent to "Deposit RLUSD for shares" and interpolatedIntent to "Pay RLUSD to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}".

findings.title: mint cannot show the RLUSD amount the signer pays; the share price sets it with no cap.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. No maxAssets parameter. Case 1: RLUSD out 1000000000 wei; the screen shows 'Deposit asset: RLUSD' only.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show the computed amount. Optionally relabel to 'Pay with (amount set by share price)'.

cases.notes: RLUSD out: the asset is named in a field, but the amount (0.000000001 RLUSD) is not shown and has no bound. The shares go to 0xdead (signer null), and the screen shows that correctly.

redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver,.worst: redeem never names RLUSD as the asset the receiver gets; the reader had to guess it.

mint(uint256 shares, address onBehalf).worst: mint intent and sentence say 'Mint' and never say that RLUSD leaves the signer's wallet.

summary.worst: redeem never names RLUSD as the asset the receiver gets; the reader had to guess it.
